Only this test class exists (28 tests total matches), confirming it's the only `*AgentTest.java` in the tree and nothing else is affected.

## Summary

Created `src/test/org/apache/commons/lang/time/DurationFormatUtilsAgentTest.java` (JUnit 3.8 style, matching the project's convention) with 28 tests covering `formatDurationHMS`, `formatDurationISO`, `formatDuration`, `formatDurationWords`, `formatPeriod`/`formatPeriodISO`, and the package-private `lexx`/`Token` helpers, including padding, no-padding, negative durations, null/empty format, and calendar-boundary cases.

25 tests pass. 3 fail, and each failure reveals a genuine bug in `DurationFormatUtils`:

1. **`testFormatDurationHMSLargeDurationHourOverflow`** — `formatDuration` (and therefore `formatDurationHMS`) casts the hours quotient `durationMillis / MILLIS_PER_HOUR` to `int`. For large durations (e.g. `Long.MAX_VALUE` ms) this silently overflows, producing a wrapped/negative hour value (`-2047687697`) instead of the true value (`2562047788015`).

2. **`testFormatDurationWordsAllZeroSuppressLeadingShouldBeEmpty`** and **`testFormatDurationWordsAllZeroBothSuppressedShouldBeEmpty`** — in the `suppressLeadingZeroElements` branch of `formatDurationWords`, the code does `tmp = StringUtils.replaceOnce(duration, " 0 minutes", ""); duration = tmp;` and *then* checks `if (tmp.length() != duration.length())`. Since `duration` was just assigned from `tmp`, that check is always false, so the final cascade step (removing a trailing `" 0 seconds"`) never runs. For an all-zero duration this leaves `"0 seconds"` in the output instead of the expected `""`.
